newsitem.title: HONG KONG: W.I. Carr confirms HK derivatives trader gone.
newsitem.headline: W.I. Carr confirms HK derivatives trader gone.

text.p: W.I. Carr confirmed on Tuesday that its former head of equity-derivatives trading in Hong Kong, Magnus Eriksson, had left the company.
"Eriksson is no longer employed by W.I. Carr," a company spokesman said. But the spokesman refused to say who had initiated Eriksson's departure or what brought it about.
Eriksson could not be reached for comment.

The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong said it was looking into unusual share market activity last Thursday and market sources said W.I. Carr was one of the six brokerage houses being asked to explain trades that day.
Local newspapers reported on Tuesday that Eriksson, who was a managing director at the firm, lost up to US$6 million last Thursday trading equity derivatives and had been sacked.
The Hang Seng Index surged 213 points to a record of 13,744.30 in the first 15 minutes of trade last Thursday but closed the day down 220.19 points at 13,310.76.
